papers.title: LncPNdeep: A long non-coding RNA classifier based on large language model with peptide and nucleotide embedding.
papers.abstract: Accurate classification of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) is essential for transcriptome annotation and understanding gene regulation. Existing computational methods predominantly rely on nucleotide sequence features, frequently overlooking biologically relevant peptide signals encoded within lncRNAs. To overcome this limitation, we developed LncPNdeep, an integrative deep learning framework that combines nucleotide and peptide embeddings extracted via masked language models, specifically utilizing contextual representations from BigBird, Longformer, and ProtTrans. By fusing both features in a
papers.summary: LncPNdeep is a new deep learning framework that classifies long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) by combining both nucleotide and peptide sequence features extracted using large language models. This approach improves classification accuracy by capturing biologically relevant peptide signals that are often missed by methods relying only on nucleotide sequences.

papers.title: Site-specific recombinases and their essential role in synthetic biology.
papers.abstract: Site-specific recombinases, enzymes that bind to specific DNA attachment sites and catalyze DNA rearrangement reactions resulting in permanent and heritable genetic modifications, have emerged as powerful tools in synthetic biology. Their broad applications in genome engineering, genetic circuit design, DNA assembly, and computational design have significantly advanced the field over the past decades. To provide a systematic overview of both fundamental concepts and recent progress, this review comprehensively summarizes site-specific recombinases across enzyme categories, structural mechanism
papers.summary: This review provides a systematic overview of site-specific recombinases, enzymes that catalyze precise DNA rearrangements, and their applications in synthetic biology, including genome engineering, genetic circuit design, and DNA assembly. It covers enzyme categories and structural mechanisms, highlighting their essential role in advancing the field.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Genomic Data Analysis: New Frontiers in Precision Medicine.
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of next-generation sequencing technologies has generated unprecedented volumes of genomic data; however, translating these data into reliable and clinically actionable insights remains a major challenge in precision medicine. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a key enabling technology across the genomic medicine pipeline, supporting variant detection, variant interpretation, polygenic risk prediction, disease subtyping, biomarker discovery and treatment-response modelling. This review provides a clinically oriented, pipeline-based synthesis of contemporary AI appl
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how artificial intelligence is being applied across the genomic medicine pipeline, from variant detection and interpretation to polygenic risk prediction and treatment-response modeling. It highlights AI as a key enabling technology for translating large-scale genomic data into clinically actionable insights in precision medicine.

papers.title: Comparative Genomic Analysis Reveals Distribution, Organization, and Evolution of Ferrous and Sulfur Oxidation Genes in the Genus Acidithiobacillus.
papers.abstract: Acidithiobacillus spp. are key players in metal mobilization and sulfur cycling in acidic environments, with important applications in biomining and bioleaching operations. But the evolutionary organization of the iron and sulfur oxidation systems of these organisms is not well understood. In this study, a comparative genomic analysis of 31 Acidithiobacillus genomes (95,180 predicted proteins) was performed to investigate the distribution, conservation, and genomic organization of genes involved in ferrous iron oxidation, reduced sulfur compound oxidation, respiratory electron transfer, and su
papers.summary: This study performs a comparative genomic analysis of 31 Acidithiobacillus genomes to map the distribution, conservation, and genomic organization of genes involved in ferrous iron and sulfur oxidation, as well as respiratory electron transfer. The findings reveal evolutionary patterns and genomic arrangements that enhance our understanding of these key biomining organisms, with potential implications for bioleaching applications.

papers.title: Deciphering chromatin architecture and dynamics in Plasmodium falciparum using the nucDetective pipeline.
papers.abstract: High-resolution analysis of cellular chromatin structure is crucial for uncovering developmental and cell-type-specific regulatory networks. We developed the nucDetective pipeline to provide a comprehensive evaluation of chromatin organisation. This involves assessing nucleosome positioning, occupancy, fuzziness, and array regularity. The pipeline was benchmarked by analysing the chromatin structure of the malaria-causing parasite Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) during its erythrocytic development cycle. Pf is characterised by a unique chromatin landscape, exhibiting unstable nucleosomes and a geno
papers.summary: The authors developed nucDetective, a computational pipeline for high-resolution analysis of chromatin structure, including nucleosome positioning, occupancy, fuzziness, and array regularity. They benchmarked it on the malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum, revealing its unique chromatin landscape with unstable nucleosomes, and providing a new tool for studying chromatin dynamics in organisms with atypical chromatin organization.

papers.title: Ion chromatography-ultra-high-resolution mass spectrometry reveals EZH2-driven reprogramming of nucleic acid and protein methylation.
papers.abstract: ENHANCER OF ZESTE: homolog 2 (EZH2), a histone H3K27 trimethyltransferase, is a key epigenetic regulator frequently dysregulated in cancer. To determine its impact on nucleotide biosynthesis and nucleic acid methylation in intact cells requires highly sensitive, isomer-resolving analytical workflows. We developed a targeted ion chromatography-ultra-high-resolution Fourier transform mass spectrometry (IC-UHR-FTMS) workflow with lower limits of quantification down to 9 fmol on-column to determine changes in methylation of DNA, total RNA, and mRNA in A549 cells following EZH2 knockdown (KD). Usin
papers.summary: This paper presents a new ion chromatography-ultra-high-resolution mass spectrometry (IC-UHR-FTMS) method that can sensitively measure nucleic acid and protein methylation changes. Using this approach, the authors show that EZH2 knockdown in A549 cells reprograms methylation patterns, revealing EZH2's broader role beyond histone modification.

papers.title: Whole Exome Sequencing Unveils Novel Pathogenic Variants in an Iranian Cohort with Retinal Dystrophies: Implications for Genetic Diagnosis and Counseling.
papers.abstract: Retinal dystrophies (RD) are a heterogeneous group of genetic disorders leading to progressive vision loss. The notable gap in the genetics of RD is primarily due to unidentified disease genes and variants. Advanced genotyping technologies present significant opportunities for the identification of causative variants, thereby contributing to improved disease management.
papers.summary: This study used whole exome sequencing to identify novel pathogenic variants in an Iranian cohort with retinal dystrophies, expanding the known genetic landscape of these disorders. The findings have implications for improving genetic diagnosis and counseling in this population.

papers.title: FERMO: A Dashboard for Biochemometric Prioritization of Molecular Features from Mass Spectral Data.
papers.abstract: Many natural products can selectively modulate biological processes, making them prime candidates for drug discovery. However, the complexity of biological samples makes clear attribution of activity to molecules challenging, thereby hampering hypothesis-driven prioritization, with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry routinely detecting hundreds of molecules per sample. Existing biochemometric tools typically focus on facilitating data-driven exploration to support manual interpretation, rather than more objective, data-driven prioritization and hypothesis generation. Here, we intro
papers.summary: FERMO is a new dashboard tool that uses biochemometric analysis to prioritize molecular features from mass spectral data, helping researchers link biological activity to specific molecules in complex samples. It provides a more objective, data-driven approach to hypothesis generation compared to existing tools that rely on manual interpretation.

papers.title: Protocol for leveraging local ancestry and cross-ancestry genetic architecture to improve polygenic prediction in admixed populations.
papers.abstract: Polygenic prediction is often less accurate in admixed populations due to limited representation in training data. Here, we present a protocol for building a polygenic prediction model using admixed populations from the All of Us program. We describe steps for variant extraction, phasing, local ancestry inference, and construction of polygenic risk score. This protocol may also serve as a useful reference for researchers aiming to conduct large-scale analysis in the All of Us Research Workbench cost-effectively. For complete details on the use and execution of the protocol, please refer to Zho
papers.summary: This protocol paper describes a method for improving polygenic risk scores in admixed populations by leveraging local ancestry information and cross-ancestry genetic architecture, using data from the All of Us program. It provides step-by-step guidance on variant extraction, phasing, local ancestry inference, and PRS construction, and offers practical tips for cost-effective large-scale analysis in the All of Us Research Workbench.

papers.title: EZmito2: a tool suite for mitochondrial genome dataset preparation, population genetics, and visualization.
papers.abstract: Mitogenomic datasets are central to molecular evolution and phylogenetics, yet preparatory workflows remain labor-intensive and prone to errors introduced during manual data preparation. EZmito2 is a re-implementation of the widely used EZmito pipeline that offers a fully reproducible, and user-accessible solution for mitogenomic dataset curation and result visualization. It is accessible via a public web-server for rapid analyses and through local installation, enabling reproducible workflows on personal computers or computational clusters. The pipeline consolidates the core modules-EZpipe, E
papers.summary: EZmito2 is an updated, user-friendly tool suite that automates mitochondrial genome dataset preparation, population genetics analysis, and visualization, reducing manual errors and improving reproducibility. It is available both as a web server and for local installation, supporting scalable workflows on personal computers or clusters.

papers.title: DNA methylation profiling enables subclassification of mucinous ovarian carcinoma and distinguishes it from extraovarian mucinous metastases.
papers.abstract: Mucinous ovarian carcinoma (MOC) is an epithelial ovarian cancer subtype that is frequently misclassified as extraovarian mucinous metastasis (EOM) because of overlapping features. To address this diagnostic challenge, we perform genome-wide DNA methylation profiling of 58 MOCs, 38 EOMs, and 18 mucinous borderline ovarian tumors (mBOTs) collected from six institutions. Methylation analysis defines two mBOT groups, one epigenetically similar to normal ovary and one resembling MOC. Unsupervised clustering reveals two distinct MOC methylation subtypes with potential prognostic relevance in the in
papers.summary: This study uses genome-wide DNA methylation profiling to distinguish mucinous ovarian carcinoma (MOC) from extraovarian mucinous metastases (EOM), a common diagnostic challenge. The analysis identifies distinct methylation subtypes of MOC with potential prognostic relevance, and shows that mucinous borderline ovarian tumors can be epigenetically classified into groups resembling normal ovary or MOC.

papers.title: Promises and Pitfalls of Long-Read Sequencing for Resolving Microbial Complexity.
papers.abstract: Long-read sequencing (LRS) has driven a transition in microbial genomics, overcoming the assembly fragmentation inherent to short-read sequencing. This review elucidates the impact of LRS across isolate genomics, metagenomics, and multi-omics domains. By spanning extensive repetitive regions, LRS facilitates the reconstruction of circular chromosomes and precisely resolves mobile genetic elements (MGEs). In metagenomics, LRS enables strain-level resolution, the recovery of circular metagenome-assembled genomes, and the precise localization of MGEs within host replicons. Furthermore, the single
papers.summary: This review discusses how long-read sequencing (LRS) is transforming microbial genomics by overcoming short-read assembly limitations, enabling complete circular chromosome reconstruction and precise resolution of mobile genetic elements. It highlights LRS benefits across isolate genomics, metagenomics, and multi-omics, including strain-level resolution and recovery of circular metagenome-assembled genomes, while also addressing current pitfalls and challenges.

papers.title: The LncRNA-Tumor Immune Microenvironment Nexus: Integrative Insights for Cancer Immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as pivotal regulators of tumor-immune interactions, bridging epigenetic, transcriptional, and post-transcriptional control of immune signaling networks. Recent multi-omics analyses reveal that lncRNAs shape the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) by influencing immune-cell differentiation, activation, and exhaustion, as well as cytokine, chemokine, and immune-checkpoint pathways. Acting through molecular scaffolding, chromatin remodeling, and competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) mechanisms, lncRNAs orchestrate the recruitment and functional polarization
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent multi-omics findings on how long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) regulate the tumor immune microenvironment, influencing immune cell behavior and checkpoint pathways. It highlights the potential of lncRNAs as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Integrated proteomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic profiling identifies SRA1 as a novel therapeutic target for postpartum depression.
papers.abstract: Postpartum depression (PPD) is among the most common complications of childbirth, and identifying novel treatments is vital. We aimed to identify potential drug targets for PPD by integrating the plasma proteome, transcriptome and epigenome. We designed a comprehensive analysis pipeline involving two-sample Mendelian randomisation (MR) (for proteins), colocalisation (for coding genes), and summary-based MR (SMR) (for mRNA and DNA methylation) to identify potential therapeutic targets for PPD. Genetic data on the plasma proteome were obtained from 4907 aptamers in 35,559 Icelanders and 7596 pro
papers.summary: This study integrates plasma proteomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic data using Mendelian randomization and colocalization analyses to identify SRA1 as a potential novel therapeutic target for postpartum depression. The findings suggest that targeting SRA1 could offer a new treatment avenue for PPD.

papers.title: Integrative genomic and proteomic analyses identify candidate genetic loci and genetically supported proteins in age-related macular degeneration.
papers.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of visual impairment; however, robust drug targets for primary prevention remain elusive. This study aimed to identify candidate genetic loci and putative genetically supported proteins for AMD through integrative genomics and proteomics.
papers.summary: This study integrates genomic and proteomic data to identify new genetic loci and proteins associated with age-related macular degeneration (AMD), offering potential drug targets for prevention. The findings highlight specific proteins with genetic support, advancing the understanding of AMD's molecular basis.

papers.title: Exploring rare coumarins biosynthesis by Gloeophyllum trabeum: an integrated computational genomics, molecular docking and spectroscopic approach.
papers.abstract: The sustained rise of antibiotics resistance demands the discovery of novel compounds to enhance current treatment efficiency and decrease the spread of resistant pathogens. Gloeophyllum trabeum is a common wood-decaying basidiomycete fungus, however its capability for production of specialised metabolites remains poorly understood. We integrated spectroscopic analysis, computational genomic, and molecular docking to explore isocoumarin biosynthesis of this mushroom. Using plate-based overlay bioassays we showed that G. trabeum is antagonistic against three microbes: Escherichia coli, Saccharo
papers.summary: This study explores the biosynthesis of rare coumarins in the wood-decaying fungus Gloeophyllum trabeum by integrating computational genomics, molecular docking, and spectroscopic analysis. The authors demonstrate that G. trabeum produces isocoumarins with antimicrobial activity against E. coli and other microbes, highlighting its potential as a source of novel antibiotic compounds.

papers.title: Deep learning enabled prediction of nuclear lamina-associated chromatin.
papers.abstract: Tethering of chromatin regions to the nuclear lamina contributes to genome organization and gene regulation. Though several molecular and epigenomic determinants of lamina association have been studied, the influence of genomic sequences has received less attention. Here, we present lamina-associated domain finder (LADDER), a multimodal deep learning model to predict lamina association based on DNA sequence, gene density, and long interspersed nuclear element (LINE)1 and short interspersed nuclear element (SINE) densities. The predictions made by LADDER are cell-type independent. Using LADDER'
papers.summary: This paper introduces LADDER, a multimodal deep learning model that predicts nuclear lamina-associated chromatin regions using DNA sequence, gene density, and LINE1/SINE repeat densities. The model provides cell-type-independent predictions, highlighting the role of genomic sequence features in chromatin organization.

papers.title: plsMD: a plasmid reconstruction tool from short-read assemblies.
papers.abstract: While whole genome sequencing has become a cornerstone of antimicrobial resistance surveillance, the reconstruction of plasmid sequences from short-read data remains a challenge due to repetitive sequences and assembly fragmentation. Current computational tools for plasmid identification and binning have limitations in reconstructing full plasmid sequences, hindering downstream analyses like phylogenetic studies and antimicrobial resistance gene tracking.
papers.summary: This paper introduces plsMD, a new computational tool designed to improve plasmid reconstruction from short-read whole-genome sequencing data, addressing challenges posed by repetitive sequences and assembly fragmentation. By enhancing the recovery of complete plasmid sequences, plsMD aims to facilitate downstream analyses such as antimicrobial resistance gene tracking and phylogenetic studies.

papers.title: Detecting somatic mutations in rare clones using single-cell multiomics.
papers.abstract: Somatic mutations are increasingly recognized as drivers of diseases beyond cancer, including autoimmune disorders. However, identifying rare, cell type-specific causal mutations remains challenging due to their low frequency within heterogeneous cell populations. Traditional bulk sequencing approaches lack the resolution to detect rare variants, underscoring the need for novel methods specifically designed for single-cell data of heterogeneous cell populations. We present an integrated single-cell multiomics computational framework, SCARCE (Single-Cell Analysis of Rare Clonal Events), tailore
papers.summary: SCARCE is a new computational framework that integrates single-cell multiomics data to detect rare somatic mutations in specific cell types, overcoming the limitations of bulk sequencing in heterogeneous populations. This approach could help identify causal mutations in diseases like autoimmune disorders.

papers.title: Uniform processing and analysis of IGVF massively parallel reporter assay data with MPRAsnakeflow.
papers.abstract: As researchers and clinicians seek to identify human genomic alterations relevant to traits and disorders, identifying and aggregating evidence providing mechanistic support for associations between alterations and phenotypes remains challenging. In particular, the study of noncoding genomic variation remains a major challenge because of the lack of accurate functional annotation for activity in a given context and across alleles. Experimental evidence is critical for prioritizing and interpreting functional effects of genetic alterations. Massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs) have emerge
papers.summary: This paper presents MPRAsnakeflow, a computational pipeline for uniformly processing and analyzing massively parallel reporter assay (MPRA) data from the Impact of Genomic Variation on Function (IGVF) consortium. The pipeline standardizes data processing, enabling consistent functional annotation of noncoding variants across studies, which is critical for interpreting disease-associated genetic alterations.

papers.title: Single cell CRISPR screen identifies antagonism between Nsd1-H3K36me2 and Ezh2-H3K27me3 orchestrates pluripotency transition.
papers.abstract: The transcriptional and epigenetic landscape imposes constraints on the self-renewal capacity and lineage specification potential of both naive and primed mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). CRISPR/Cas9-based functional screening coupled with single-cell RNA-seq (CROP-seq) establishes relationships between gRNA-mediated knockout genotype and transcriptome phenotype, providing a powerful tool to dissect gene regulatory networks. Here, we employed CROP-seq to investigate the epigenetic regulation governing the pluripotency network in mESCs. This highly sensitive method identified key genes essen
papers.summary: This study uses CROP-seq, a single-cell CRISPR screen, to identify epigenetic regulators essential for the naive-to-primed pluripotency transition in mouse embryonic stem cells. The screen reveals an antagonistic relationship between Nsd1-mediated H3K36me2 and Ezh2-mediated H3K27me3, which orchestrates the transcriptional and epigenetic changes required for this transition.

papers.title: Lineage-associated small inversions disrupt dosT, dnaE2, and a promoter-adjacent region in some Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.
papers.abstract: Large molecular inversions in the genome of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) due to factors like the presence of insertion sequences and transposases are widely known. However, smaller inversions within coding sequences and non-coding control elements are rarely reported. The present study aims to identify inversions and their potential impact on Mtb biology in a lineage-specific manner. Structural variants (SVs) could only be detected by long reads. For this, we simulated long reads by de novo assembling the short-read sequencing data sets and subsequently aligned representative strains from
papers.summary: This study identifies small genomic inversions in Mycobacterium tuberculosis that disrupt the dosT, dnaE2 genes and a promoter-adjacent region in a lineage-specific manner. Using simulated long reads from short-read data, the authors reveal that these small structural variants may impact Mtb biology, highlighting a previously underappreciated source of genetic variation.

papers.title: A chromosome-level genome assembly of Platycladus orientalis and comparative genomics reveal pivotal roles of transposable elements in gene duplication and pseudogenization across gymnosperm giga-genomes.
papers.abstract: Gymnosperms, particularly conifers, exhibit a high abundance of transposable elements (TEs) in their giga-scale genomes. TEs interact both antagonistically and cooperatively with the host genome, promoting structural and genetic innovations across evolutionary lineages. However, how TEs shape the coding space of gymnosperm genomes remains a key unresolved question. Here, we present a high-quality genome assembly for the keystone conifer Platycladus orientalis, with a contig N50 of 57.54 Mb-the highest continuity reported to date-to investigate the role of TEs. Comparative genomics confirms the
papers.summary: This study presents a high-quality, chromosome-level genome assembly of Platycladus orientalis with the highest contig continuity reported for a conifer, and uses comparative genomics to reveal that transposable elements have played pivotal roles in gene duplication and pseudogenization across gymnosperm giga-genomes. The findings provide new insights into how TEs shape the coding space of these massive genomes.

papers.title: ZATELLITE: a toolkit to visualize and manipulate human centromeres in live cells using synthetic zinc fingers.
papers.abstract: Changes in the number of chromosomes or their spatial organization within the nucleus have critical consequences for cell fate. Yet capturing the karyotype or three-dimensional architecture of chromatin in living cells remains limited by the difficulty in labeling endogenous loci non-invasively. The most widely used tools rely on dCas9, a bulky protein whose persistent DNA binding interferes with DNA and RNA metabolism, causes DNA damage, and is hard to multiplex. We developed ZATELLITE , an AI-enabled tool to target endogenous repetitive sequences with fluorescently-tagged synthetic zinc fing
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: ZATELLITE is a new toolkit that uses AI-designed synthetic zinc fingers to fluorescently label and manipulate human centromeres in live cells, offering a more compact and less disruptive alternative to dCas9-based methods. It enables non-invasive visualization of chromosome number and nuclear architecture, with potential for multiplexing and reduced DNA damage.

papers.title: DNA Methylation Signatures of Upper Aerodigestive Tract Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Sarcomatoid Squamous Cell Carcinoma Are Similar: A Potential Novel Diagnostic Tool for the Diagnosis of Sarcomatoid Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Upper aerodigestive tract squamous cell carcinoma (UATSCC) is often easy to recognize in its conventional form. However, a subset of tumors loses histologic evidence of squamous differentiation and, instead, become sarcomatoid (spindled). These cases may be difficult or impossible to appropriately classify on biopsy material, even with immunohistochemistry. DNA methylation has emerged as a tool to help in classifying undifferentiated malignancies. We sought to explore whether conventional and sarcomatoid UATSCC harbor the same epigenetic signature.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether conventional and sarcomatoid (spindled) upper aerodigestive tract squamous cell carcinomas share similar DNA methylation profiles. The findings suggest that the epigenetic signatures are similar, indicating that DNA methylation analysis could serve as a diagnostic tool for challenging sarcomatoid cases that are difficult to classify by histology or immunohistochemistry.

papers.title: Methylation clocks fail to generalize across genetically admixed individuals.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic aging clocks based on DNA methylation patterns across the genome have emerged as a potential biomarker for risk of age-related diseases, like Alzheimer's disease (AD), and environmental and social stressors. However, methylation clocks have not been comprehensively validated in genetically diverse individuals. Here, we evaluate a set of first-, second-, and third-generation methylation clocks in 621 AD patients and matched controls from African American, Hispanic, and White cohorts. The clocks are less accurate at predicting age in genetically admixed cohorts compared to the White c
papers.summary: This study evaluates the accuracy of epigenetic aging clocks across genetically diverse cohorts and finds that they perform worse in admixed populations (African American and Hispanic) compared to White individuals. The results highlight a critical limitation in current methylation clocks, which may bias age-related disease risk assessments in non-European populations.

papers.title: Fine-grained structural classification of biosynthetic gene cluster-encoded products.
papers.abstract: Biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) are responsible the biosynthesis of many natural products, including a multitude of effective therapeutics and their precursors. Advances in genomic data collection as well as computational techniques have made it possible to identify BGCs at scale. However, accurately determining the types of BGC-encoded products from genomic content remains elusive.
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational method for fine-grained structural classification of products encoded by biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), addressing the challenge of accurately determining product types from genomic data. The approach improves upon existing tools by enabling more detailed categorization, which could aid in natural product discovery.

papers.title: ECLIPSE: exploring the dark proteome of ESKAPE pathogens through the sequence similarity network of the Protein Universe Atlas.
papers.abstract: The accelerating crisis of antimicrobial resistance among the critical so-called ESKAPE pathogens demands the urgent identification of novel molecular targets. However, a substantial fraction of ESKAPE proteomes remains functionally uncharacterized, with many genes annotated as encoding hypothetical proteins. These protein sequences often lack significant similarity to known protein families when conventional homology-based annotation methods are used and thus remain "dark". This limits our ability to explore their roles in pathogenicity, and it is thus crucial to bridge this substantial gap i
papers.summary: This paper introduces ECLIPSE, a computational approach that leverages the sequence similarity network of the Protein Universe Atlas to functionally annotate the 'dark proteome' of ESKAPE pathogens—proteins with no known function. By exploring these uncharacterized proteins, ECLIPSE aims to identify novel molecular targets to combat antimicrobial resistance.

papers.title: Partial Reproducibility and Pleiotropic Epigenetic QTLs in Arabidopsis Recombinant Inbred Lines.
papers.abstract: Unlike conventional genetic polymorphisms, many induced epigenetic polymorphisms can be reset across generations, raising uncertainty about how consistently the same epigenetic loci and associated phenotypic effects can be recovered among independent studies. To address this problem, we designed our study specifically to maximize a lineage-matched, environmentally aligned cross-study comparability with the foundational work of Cortijo et al. by using seeds derived from the same epiRIL generation and grown under broadly similar environmental conditions. We mapped flowering time, as well as five
papers.summary: This study investigates the reproducibility of epigenetic quantitative trait loci (epiQTLs) in Arabidopsis recombinant inbred lines, finding only partial overlap with a foundational study despite careful experimental matching. The results reveal pleiotropic effects of epigenetic loci on flowering time and other traits, highlighting the context-dependent nature of epigenetic variation.

papers.title: Assessing the influence of different alignment tools on the accuracy of a forensic epigenetic clock.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation (DNAm) has long been a commonly investigated biomarker in biomedical research. The current gold standard for DNAm detection is bisulfite sequencing which requires dedicated alignment tools that can handle reduced sequence complexity. One commonly used application of DNAm are epigenetic clock measurements. These clocks have been adapted by many fields for their specific needs, including forensic genetics. Here, epigenetic clocks were designed to help estimate the chronological age of a biological stain donor for investigative purposes.
papers.summary: This study evaluates how different alignment tools affect the accuracy of a forensic epigenetic clock, which estimates the age of a biological sample donor from DNA methylation data. The authors compare multiple bisulfite sequencing aligners and find that tool choice can significantly impact clock accuracy, highlighting the need for standardized alignment protocols in forensic applications.

papers.title: Conserved Core and Species-Specific Signatures in the Milk Exosomal microRNA Targetome: A Preliminary Comparative In Silico Analysis of Human, Cow, Goat and Donkey Milk.
papers.abstract: Milk-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) transport microRNAs (miRNAs) that are unusually stable and have been proposed to survive digestion and modulate gene expression in the consumer, although their dietary bioavailability and physiological relevance remain debated. How the predicted regulatory potential of these miRNAs differs among the milks of different animals most relevant to human nutrition has not been systematically compared. Here, we performed an integrative in silico analysis of publicly available small-RNA sequencing data from 29 milk and milk-cell samples of human, cow, goat, an
papers.summary: This study computationally compared the microRNA targetomes of milk-derived extracellular vesicles from human, cow, goat, and donkey, identifying conserved core regulatory targets as well as species-specific signatures. The findings suggest that while some miRNA-mediated effects may be shared across species, each milk type also has unique potential to influence consumer gene expression, highlighting the need for further experimental validation.

papers.title: A portable recalibration workflow for reference-based variant calling in non-human genomes.
papers.abstract: A key computational step in reference-based variant calling is distinguishing true genetic variants from sequencing errors. Advanced tools and workflows have been developed to handle this by computational modelling of technical errors from the sequencing machines. However, these recalibration workflows have largely been evaluated for human data only and its exact applicability for non-human data remains unknown. Here, we conducted a systematic evaluation of variant calling on human, rice, sheep, and chickpea data, and found that existing workflows introduce unexpected statistical bias, thus le
papers.summary: This study evaluates the performance of existing variant-calling recalibration workflows on non-human genomes (rice, sheep, chickpea) compared to human data, revealing that these workflows introduce unexpected statistical bias when applied to non-human species. The authors propose a portable recalibration workflow that corrects this bias, improving the accuracy of reference-based variant calling across diverse genomes.

papers.title: Integrative in silico and in vitro screening of small molecules targeting RNA.
papers.abstract: Targeting structured RNA elements with small molecules has emerged as a promising yet technically challenging strategy for antiviral drug discovery. Here, we present a comprehensive and experimentally validated workflow for the integrative in silico and in vitro screening of RNA-binding small molecules. The approach is exemplified using conserved RNA elements from the SARS-CoV-2 genome, including the 5'-terminal stem-loop 1 and the programmed -1 ribosomal frameshift pseudoknot, but is broadly applicable to other structured RNAs. The workflow integrates high-resolution RNA structural ensemble g
papers.summary: This protocol paper presents a validated workflow that combines computational screening with in vitro assays to identify small molecules targeting structured RNA elements, demonstrated on SARS-CoV-2 RNA motifs. It offers a broadly applicable approach for RNA-targeted drug discovery, integrating structural ensemble modeling with experimental validation.

papers.title: Genomic epidemiology reveals geographically structured co-circulation of AFR10 and AFR13 Vibrio cholerae lineages driving cholera outbreaks in Tanzania (2022-2024).
papers.abstract: Cholera remains a persistent public health challenge in Tanzania, with recurrent outbreaks across multiple regions overwhelming the health systems. Despite the ongoing surveillance to control the transmission, limited genomic characterization of circulating Vibrio cholerae strains has constrained traceability of outbreak sources and transmission dynamics including virulence determinants and antimicrobial resistance profiles to guide clinical and public health interventions. We conducted a genome analysis of 144 archived isolates from 2022 to 2024 cholera outbreaks from 16 regions across Tanzan
papers.summary: This study used genomic epidemiology to analyze 144 Vibrio cholerae isolates from 2022-2024 cholera outbreaks across 16 regions in Tanzania, revealing geographically structured co-circulation of two distinct lineages (AFR10 and AFR13). The findings provide crucial insights into outbreak sources, transmission dynamics, and antimicrobial resistance profiles, which can inform targeted public health interventions in Tanzania.

papers.title: Transcriptome datasets of salicylic acid-treated tomato plant cultures under normal and stress conditions.
papers.abstract: Extreme weather events pose a significant challenge to agricultural systems, as they induce various abiotic stress responses in plants. Preventive crop protection strategies that aim to enhance plant resistance in advance are gaining increasing importance to mitigate these stress effects. Priming treatments based on the activation of the immune response allow plants to be prepared for stress by triggering some of the defense mechanisms before the actual stress occurs. In the study, healthy, young tomato plants were pre-treated with a foliar spray containing salicylic acid and then subjected to
papers.summary: This dataset provides transcriptome profiles of tomato plants treated with salicylic acid under normal and stress conditions, enabling study of priming-induced stress resistance. It supports research on preventive crop protection strategies against abiotic stress.

papers.title: An alignment-free strategy for circulating tumor DNA detection and tumor fraction estimation from whole-genome sequencing data.
papers.abstract: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is emerging as a promising biomarker for postoperative monitoring of cancer patients. Precise estimation of circulating tumor fraction is crucial for evaluating treatment effects and timely detection of disease recurrence. All current ctDNA detection methods that utilize whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data rely on the reference genome alignment of sequencing reads and often apply separate tools for detecting different variant types. However, various bioinformatic analysis confounders and the application of external variant calling tools could be avoided by analyzin
papers.summary: This paper introduces an alignment-free method for detecting circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and estimating tumor fraction directly from whole-genome sequencing data, bypassing the need for reference genome alignment and external variant callers. By avoiding alignment, the approach reduces bioinformatic confounders and simplifies the analysis pipeline, potentially improving accuracy and speed for postoperative cancer monitoring.

papers.title: DNA Methylation Profiling in IDH-Mutant Gliomas: Biological Evolution, Molecular Grading and Clinical Implementation.
papers.abstract: Mutations in isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 or 2 (IDH1/2) define a major subgroup of adult-type diffuse gliomas and induce accumulation of D-2-hydroxyglutarate, resulting in extensive DNA and histone methylation changes. This epigenetic reprogramming underlies the glioma CpG island methylator phenotype (G-CIMP) and contributes to tumour lineage, differentiation state and clinical behaviour. DNA methylation profiling has consequently evolved from a research tool into an important ancillary method for CNS tumour classification, molecular subclassification and copy-number analysis. This narrative rev
papers.summary: This review discusses how DNA methylation profiling has become a key tool for classifying IDH-mutant gliomas, aiding in molecular grading and clinical management. It highlights the role of epigenetic reprogramming in tumor behavior and the transition of methylation analysis from research to clinical practice.

papers.title: Accurate detection of cholangiocarcinoma in primary sclerosing cholangitis using DNA methylation biomarkers in bile and plasma.
papers.abstract: Current methods for cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) detection in primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) lack accuracy, often leading to late, non-curative diagnoses. In this study, we aim at identifying DNA methylation biomarkers in liquid biopsies for earlier and more accurate CCA detection.
papers.summary: This study identifies DNA methylation biomarkers in bile and plasma that can accurately detect cholangiocarcinoma in patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis, potentially enabling earlier and more precise diagnosis compared to current methods.

papers.title: Genome-wide DNA methylation analysis of pediatric medulloblastomas from a Brazilian cohort: an exploratory study.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation profiling is a central tool for molecular classification of pediatric medulloblastoma. However, most reference datasets are derived from high-income countries, and the performance of established epigenetic markers in underrepresented populations remains insufficiently explored.
papers.journal: Clinical & translational oncology : official publication of the Federation of Spanish Oncology Societies and of the National Cancer Institute of Mexico
papers.summary: This study performs genome-wide DNA methylation analysis on pediatric medulloblastomas from a Brazilian cohort, an underrepresented population, to evaluate whether established epigenetic classification markers perform reliably outside high-income country reference datasets. The findings provide exploratory evidence on the applicability of these markers in diverse genetic backgrounds, addressing a gap in global molecular classification equity.

papers.title: Dysregulation of piRNA biogenesis-associated proteins in cancer: mechanisms, evidence, and translational constraints.
papers.abstract: PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs), PIWI proteins, and piRNA biogenesis-associated proteins form a conserved RNA network that protects germline genome integrity and is increasingly linked to cancer biology. Most cancer reviews have emphasized altered piRNA abundance or PIWI expression, whereas the upstream machinery that generates, loads, trims, and stabilizes piRNAs has received less critical attention. For the RNA Networks and Biology section, this Review re-evaluates piRNA biogenesis proteins as RNA-network regulators rather than as isolated tumor biomarkers. We summarize the biochemical logic
papers.summary: This review reframes the role of piRNA biogenesis machinery in cancer, arguing that upstream proteins involved in piRNA generation and processing should be viewed as RNA-network regulators rather than isolated biomarkers. It summarizes the biochemical logic and evidence linking dysregulation of these proteins to cancer, while highlighting translational constraints.

papers.title: Identification and prenatal diagnosis of a novel likely pathogenic ANOS1 variant in a large Chinese Kallmann syndrome family.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to systematically analyze a Chinese family with Kallmann syndrome (KS), evaluate the pathogenicity of a candidate variant through co-segregation analysis and bioinformatic predictions, and provide clinical intervention for the family.
papers.summary: This study identifies a novel likely pathogenic variant in the ANOS1 gene in a large Chinese family with Kallmann syndrome, confirmed through co-segregation analysis and bioinformatic predictions. The findings enabled prenatal diagnosis and genetic counseling for the family, expanding the known mutation spectrum of ANOS1-related KS.

papers.title: A machine learning framework for predictive interpretation of variants of uncertain significance in hereditary cancer.
papers.abstract: Variant interpretation remains a major bottleneck in clinical genomics, with variants of uncertain significance (VUS) representing a critical unresolved challenge due to insufficient evidence for definitive classification. Existing in silico tools exhibit variable and often inconsistent performance complicating clinical decision-making, particularly in the context of hereditary cancer genomics.
papers.summary: This paper presents a machine learning framework designed to improve the predictive interpretation of variants of uncertain significance (VUS) in hereditary cancer genes. The framework aims to address the inconsistency of existing in silico tools by providing more reliable classification, which could aid clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Genome-wide identification and expression analysis of nucleotide-binding site leucine-rich repeat genes associated with downy mildew resistance in spinach.
papers.abstract: Downy mildew is a destructive disease that causes severe losses in spinach (Spinacia oleracea L.) yield and quality. Nucleotide-binding site-leucine-rich repeat (NBS-LRR) genes are core regulators of plant innate immunity and play critical roles in defense against pathogen infection. However, the characteristics of NBS-LRR family genes in spinach and their specific functions in downy mildew resistance remain unclear, limiting the development of resistant spinach cultivars.
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes the NBS-LRR gene family in spinach at the genome-wide level, and analyzes their expression patterns in response to downy mildew infection. The findings provide a foundation for understanding the roles of these immune receptor genes in spinach resistance and for developing resistant cultivars.

papers.title: Simultaneous detection of thalassemia, hemoglobinopathies, and G6PD variants using long-read nanopore sequencing: genetic complexity and heterogeneity in Thailand.
papers.abstract: Thalassemia, hemoglobinopathies, and glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency represent highly prevalent and genetically heterogeneous inherited hematologic disorders or diseases in Thailand. Conventional molecular approaches require multiple targeted assays to detect deletional and non-deletional variants across globin gene clusters and the G6PD gene, resulting in increased complexity, turnaround time, and cost. We developed and analytically validated a comprehensive long-read sequencing workflow using Oxford Nanopore Technologies for simultaneous detection of pathogenic variants i
papers.summary: This study presents a long-read nanopore sequencing workflow that simultaneously detects thalassemia, hemoglobinopathies, and G6PD deficiency variants in a single assay, addressing the genetic heterogeneity common in Thailand. The approach simplifies molecular diagnosis by replacing multiple targeted tests, potentially reducing cost and turnaround time.

papers.title: Immunogenomic profiling reveals targets for gene therapy in pediatric brain tumors.
papers.abstract: Pediatric brain tumors, particularly pontine diffuse midline glioma (pDMG), remains lethal with limited therapeutic options. Improved stereotactic biopsy techniques and advances in bioinformatics are progressively enabling deeper exploration of immunological vulnerabilities empowering novel strategies, including adoptive cell and gene therapies (ACGTs). We aimed to integrate genomic, transcriptomic, and immunological analyses to identify actionable pathways, surface antigens, and neoantigens that could inform next-generation immunotherapies, including Chimetic Antigen Receptor (CAR)-T cells an
papers.summary: This study integrates genomic, transcriptomic, and immunological profiling of pediatric brain tumors, especially pontine diffuse midline glioma (pDMG), to identify actionable targets for adoptive cell and gene therapies such as CAR-T cells. The authors uncover specific surface antigens and neoantigens that could inform next-generation immunotherapies for these lethal tumors.

papers.title: Genomic evolution and minority variant dynamics of RSV during the first season of nirsevimab implementation in Italy (2024-5).
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a leading cause of hospitalization despite the recent implementation of infant immunoprophylaxis programs. The inter- and intrahost levels of genetic variation across the genome have not been extensively investigated. Hence, the aim of this study was to characterize the whole genome of RSV strains circulating within two Italian areas during the 2024-5 RSV season, corresponding to the first season after implementation of the national nirsevimab prophylaxis program. Whole genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on 88 respiratory samples that tested positiv
papers.summary: This study sequenced 88 RSV genomes from two Italian regions during the first season of nirsevimab prophylaxis, revealing genomic evolution and minority variant dynamics. The findings provide early insights into how the immunoprophylaxis program may influence RSV genetic diversity and potential escape variants.

papers.title: Drug sensitivity prediction across cancer types using graph isomorphism networks and biological pathway features: A dual-branch deep learning approach.
papers.abstract: Drug sensitivity prediction is an important issue within the precision medicine field. IC50, which is the molar drug dose needed to decrease the viability of cells by half compared to the drug-free control, is the main pharmacodynamics parameter used for drug sensitivity analysis in large-scale pharmacogenomics screenings. Computational estimation of IC50s based on molecular and genomic factors significantly reduces costs associated with experiments for measuring cell viability and allows for accelerating the process of drug discovery. Traditional methods of IC50 calculation do not allow integ
papers.summary: This paper presents a dual-branch deep learning model that combines graph isomorphism networks with biological pathway features to predict drug sensitivity (IC50) across cancer types. The approach improves prediction accuracy by integrating molecular and genomic data, offering a cost-effective computational alternative to experimental drug sensitivity testing.

papers.title: Dietary sulforaphane in cancer chemoprevention: epigenetic regulation and PRMT5-MEP50 complex inhibition-a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Cancer chemoprevention using dietary bioactive compounds has emerged as a promising, cost-effective strategy to reduce global cancer incidence and mortality. Sulforaphane (SFN), an isothiocyanate abundant in cruciferous vegetables, has attracted considerable attention for its pleiotropic anticancer effects.
papers.summary: This systematic review consolidates evidence that dietary sulforaphane (SFN) from cruciferous vegetables exerts chemopreventive effects through epigenetic regulation and inhibition of the PRMT5-MEP50 complex, a key driver of tumorigenesis. The findings highlight SFN's potential as a cost-effective dietary strategy for cancer prevention, though further clinical validation is needed.

papers.title: The TCN1 Paradox: Unraveling the Dual Role of Transcobalamin I in Colorectal Cancer-From Metabolic Regulation to Oncogenic Signaling.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer mortality. While genetic drivers are well-characterized, epigenetic alterations-particularly DNA methylation-are increasingly recognized as critical contributors. The vitamin B12 transporter Transcobalamin I (TCN1) has recently emerged as an epigenetically regulated gene with context-dependent oncogenic functions.
papers.summary: This review discusses the emerging dual role of Transcobalamin I (TCN1) in colorectal cancer, highlighting how its epigenetic regulation (via DNA methylation) and context-dependent oncogenic functions link vitamin B12 metabolism to cancer signaling. The authors propose that TCN1 acts as a paradoxical player, both supporting metabolic needs and promoting tumor progression, and suggest it as a potential biomarker or therapeutic target.
